summary.text: St. Martha was the wife of St. Dovmont-Timothy of Pskov and entered monastic life after his death.

blocks.text: St. Martha was known in secular life as Maria. The historical ecclesiastical account identifies her as a daughter of a Russian grand prince and granddaughter of St. Alexander Nevsky. She married the ruler of Pskov, St. Dovmont-Timothy.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

sections.title: From princely household to monastic life

blocks.text: After her husband’s death, she entered the monastery of St. John the Baptist in Pskov. The historical account uses her monastic title, schemanun, and records her name as Martha. It does not provide a detailed account of her daily work or justify supplying imagined conversations or personal motives.

blocks.text: The same historical entry places her death in 1300 and records the existence of a tomb inscription identifying her as a right-believing princess and schemanun. It does not describe martyrdom or establish a medical cause of death.

blocks.text: The OCA names his wife as the future Schemanun Martha, gives November 8 as her commemoration and describes the couple on the Murozh icon. This is not the biblical Martha.
